stem:
A 34-year-old clinician recovers from influenza. Four winters later, immune testing shows poor recognition of a newly circulating strain. Surveillance indicates that the strain changed gradually across successive seasons rather than appearing as a wholly new subtype in one abrupt event.

Which of the following molecular findings most directly explains the reduced recognition of the newer strain?

options.label: A
options.text: Stable integration of viral RNA into the clinician’s genome
options.misconception: Attributes seasonal antigen change to persistence in host DNA.
options.explanation: The serial isolates instead show accumulating viral-gene mutations that alter HA and NA.

options.label: B
options.text: Abrupt exchange of viral genes in a single event
options.misconception: Chooses a sudden change despite the incremental sequence findings.
options.explanation: The passage defines drift as small mutations accumulating over time, matching the gradual pattern here.

options.label: C
options.text: Progressive deletion of surface-antigen genes without replacement
options.misconception: Mistakes altered antigens for loss of the antigen-encoding genes.
options.explanation: The findings show changing HA and NA produced by small mutations, not disappearance of their genes.

options.label: D
options.text: Accumulation of point changes that alter surface antigens
options.misconception: Recognizes the gradual molecular pattern of antigenic drift.
options.explanation: Antigenic drift is the accumulation of small viral-gene mutations that progressively change HA and NA.

options.label: E
options.text: Selection by antibodies without changes in viral genes
options.misconception: Ignores the directly observed viral sequence changes.
options.explanation: Immune recognition falls because mutations change HA and NA; unchanged viral genes would not match the data.

context: Learning objective: recognize antigenic drift from serial change. Small mutations accumulate in influenza genes, changing HA and NA until older immune recognition becomes less effective; the incremental pattern distinguishes drift from a single abrupt event.
